title: The maximal metabolic steady state: redefining the 'gold standard'
claims: Maximal lactate steady state (MLSS) is operationally defined as the highest power output at which blood lactate rises by less than 1 mmol/L between 10 and 30 minutes of constant exercise.
MLSS was historically assumed to occur at a fixed blood lactate concentration of 2.2 mmol/L or, more often, 4 mmol/L.

The absolute blood lactate concentration at MLSS varies considerably between individuals and between exercise modalities, so MLSS is now defined by the highest sustainable intensity rather than by a fixed lactate value.
MLSS determination is protocol-dependent: 30-minute exercise bouts produce lower power outputs at MLSS than 20-minute bouts.
Conventional MLSS testing requires a series of typically four to five 30-minute constant-load bouts on separate days.
